hints: Focus on the chloride clue first, since Period 3 elements in Groups 13 to 15 have very different chlorides.
Remember that $\text{SiCl}_4$ is a colourless liquid, while $\text{AlCl}_3$ and $\text{PCl}_5$ are white solids that hydrolyse to strongly acidic solutions.
Once you know Y must be aluminium, use the melting point order and the down-a-group fall in ionisation energy to check X.
walkthrough:
**Pin down Y and Z from the chloride test**

Y and Z are both in Period 3 and in Groups 13, 14 or 15. So they must be two of $\text{Al}$, $\text{Si}$ and $\text{P}$.

Both form white solid chlorides that give pH < 4 with water:
$$\text{AlCl}_3(s) + 6\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow [\text{Al}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+} + 3\text{Cl}^- \text{ then hydrolysis gives H}^+$$
$$\text{PCl}_5(s) + 4\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{H}_3\text{PO}_4 + 5\text{HCl}$$
$\text{SiCl}_4$ is a colourless liquid, not a white solid, so Si cannot be Y or Z. That leaves Y and Z as $\text{Al}$ and $\text{P}$ in some order.

**Use melting point to decide which is Y**

We are told melting point of Z is less than melting point of Y.

Think of structures. $\text{Al}$ is a metallic lattice with a high melting point (about $660^{\circ}\text{C}$). $\text{P}$ is simple molecular $\text{P}_4$ with a very low melting point (about $44^{\circ}\text{C}$).

So to have mp(Z) < mp(Y), we must have:
$$\text{Z} = \text{P} \text{ and Y} = \text{Al}$$

**Use group and ionisation energy to find X**

X is in the same group as Y, so X is also Group 13. First ionisation energy falls down a group because the outer electron is further from the nucleus and more shielded.

So for X to have a greater first ionisation energy than Y ($\text{Al}$), X must be above $\text{Al}$ in Group 13. That is boron:
$$\text{IE}_1(\text{B}) > \text{IE}_1(\text{Al})$$
This matches row A with X = B, Y = Al.

options.A: Y = Al gives a white solid $\text{AlCl}_3$ that hydrolyses acidic, and Z = P gives white solid $\text{PCl}_5$ that hydrolyses acidic. Melting point P < Al is correct. X = B is same Group 13 as Al and has higher first ionisation energy because it is higher up the group. All conditions fit.
options.B: Y = Si fails the chloride test. $\text{SiCl}_4$ is a colourless fuming liquid, not a white solid. Students choosing this focus only on same group (Group 14) and IE fall, but miss the white solid detail.
options.C: Y = P could give a white solid $\text{PCl}_5$, but then Z would have to be Al to satisfy the chloride test, and mp(Al) is not less than mp(P). Also X = As is below P in Group 15, so $\text{IE}_1(\text{As}) < \text{IE}_1(\text{P})$, opposite to the required X > Y.
options.D: X = N above Y = P does correctly give $\text{IE}_1(\text{N}) > \text{IE}_1(\text{P})$, which is tempting. However Y = P fails the melting point logic, because Z would then be Al and mp(Al) > mp(P), not less. So the pair cannot work together.
